parts:
Dear Rob,

Thank you very much for this reply. Your post made me understand what I =
am doing wrong.
It appears, I have wrongly used the =E2=80=9CObject to model=E2=80=9D =
control in the pull down menu of the DS model definition properties. I =
had wrongly understood that I have to use =E2=80=9Cclusters=E2=80=9D if =
I have data structured as clusters. As a result, I was modelling =
abundance of clusters not individuals. I changed the setting to =
=E2=80=9Csingle=E2=80=9D and got the results what I had been expecting =
=E2=80=93 predicted total abundance is similar to results of MRDS =
analysis and also range of predicted densities in grid cells is as =
expected.
As this solves my problem, I post this also to the list for others that =
may run into similar problem.
And thanks also to Falk, Eric and Natalia whose comments also were =
helpful.

best wishes
Ainars

From: Rob Williams=20
Sent: Tuesday, August 21, 2012 2:57 PM
To: ainars...@LU.LV=20
Subject: Re: [DIST-SAMP] Problems with predicted abundance values in =
DSM=E2=80=8F=20

Hi Ainars,=20
You say that you "assume" that density units are birds per m^2. You =
know that when you specify your model, there's a pull down menu for =
"individuals" or "clusters" right (aka "schools" or groups"). =
Similarly, when you look at the summary of your model in the outputs, it =
will tell you if you're estimating abundance of individuals or groups. =
Does that explain the difference? =20

Best,
Rob
